terms.gloss: do wrong, be naughty: male facis, that’s naughty of you
evidence: Plaut. Merc. 873: Male facis, properantem quī mē commorāre.
terms.comment: Latin scolds the act rather than the child: male facis, “you’re doing wrong”, or improbē fēcistī.

phrases.english: You rascal! What have you done?

phrases.latin: Male facis, properantem quī mē commorāre.
phrases.english: That’s naughty of you, holding me up when I’m in a hurry.

phrases.latin: prōtinus ergō, nē quid cupidē, nē quid improbē, nē quid impotenter faciat, monendus est puer
phrases.english: so from the start the boy must be warned not to do anything greedily, naughtily, or without self-control
That was naughty; it isn’t nice.

sources: Lewis & Short: improbus · Lewis & Short: petulans
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 149, 275, 350.
